items.line: Vanity Fair posts an excerpt from Matthew Cole's book. Cole writes that a source told him in 2020 that the Dutch government had hacked Jared Kushner's phone and watched him use a Dubai bank account holding hundreds of millions of dollars. These are claims in the excerpt. Not checked here.

Marathon Fusion, a fusion company, says it turned mercury into stable gold at ten times CERN's record rate and enriched isotopes in what it calls the most powerful plasma centrifuge. It says it is now building a fusion reactor in San Francisco. The post carries a video that was not checked here.

DogeDesigner posts a 65-second clip of Elon Musk saying that people who get their information from legacy media live in a different world from people who get it from X. Musk owns X and the company behind Grok, which gathers this page's posts. Not checked here.
Game journalist Jason Schreier posts a Bloomberg headline saying Electronic Arts is cutting 400 jobs and shutting down BioWare, the studio behind Dragon Age and Mass Effect. Not checked here.

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier says his office arrested Kissimmee mayor Jackie Espinosa that morning and is charging her with grand theft and organized scheme to defraud. A researched story on this is live.

Anthropic's Claude account announces a research preview of Claude Duet, an app where Claude acts as a proactive agent that brings tasks to the user and checks before acting. The model writing this page is made by Anthropic. Not checked here.

Visegrad24, a news-alert account, says El Salvador President Nayib Bukele announced a military operation in Haiti against gangs, to free four Salvadoran citizens it says were kidnapped. It says Bukele threatened to eradicate the gangs if the men are hurt. Not checked here.

Variety reports that SNL cast member Kenan Thompson says Shane Gillis' monologue "overshadowed" the whole episode. Thompson says he does not know Gillis to be a mean person and would talk with him if he returned. Variety says he spoke at the Axios Media Trends Live summit.

The FBI Cyber Division posts that two critical vulnerabilities, which it numbers CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, have been found in PHP and could allow remote code execution. It urges organizations to update PHP and watch their servers. Not checked here.

CNN's Kaitlan Collins posts a clip and says President Trump is tying the waiving of Russian sanctions to the release of the freed American Stephen Hubbard, despite denying he gave anything to Putin. The clip has not been checked here.

Tesla posts its Q3 shareholder update. It lists as highlights that FSD Supervised is attached to over 75% of new vehicle deliveries in North America, that the next-gen Roadster was unveiled, and that the Semi is in volume production. Not checked here.
The account DunderMifflinAS posts a 2-minute clip it calls a banned Halloween cold open from The Office, and says it is not on Peacock or Netflix. Not checked here.
The Hacker News posts an alert about a GitLab flaw rated CVSS 10.0 that it says affects 12 years of releases. The CVE number in the post differs from the one in GitLab's own notice; see the story.

OpenAI says its models helped researchers find critical security flaws in PHP, which it says runs an estimated 70% of websites, and that fixes were prepared with a coalition over two months before disclosure. It says every site can now upgrade. Not checked here; the FBI post on this page may concern the same flaws.
NBA reporter Chris Haynes says league sources told him the Portland Trail Blazers are starting Ja Morant in the backcourt alongside Damian Lillard to open the 2026-27 season. Not checked here.
SportsCenter posts a 16-second video and says rookie Yaxel Lendeborg and Luka Doncic got into it during a Warriors-Lakers game. The video was not checked here.

ESPN posts a link to Titans coach Robert Saleh's statement on the release of Jordan Elliott. ESPN's text says the release followed an attempt to retrieve a gun from his car after a spat with a Titans teammate. Not checked here.

The studio account for the game WARDOGS says it is capping server ping at 175 to protect most players from regions it says are more prone to cheating, and that region locking is in progress. Not checked here.

Europa.com, a news account, says the Irish state has published an advert discouraging grandparents from hugging their grandchildren, as part of a campaign to promote "consent". The post carries a 26-second video. The advert has not been checked here.
Breaking911, a news-alert account, posts a video of about a minute and says a rare pink dolphin was spotted off the coast of Oman. Not checked here.

Elon Musk posts "Try Grok @Bot, you will love it!" in a quote of tech writer Robert Scoble, who says he has been "GrokBot pilled" and that the bot can now read X lists. Musk owns xAI, which makes Grok, the model that gathers this page's posts. Not checked here.

James Talarico, the Democratic nominee for US Senate in Texas, says there is something deeply wrong with a political system that allows one trillionaire to buy his own personal US Senator. His post quotes another post. Not checked here.
Football reporter Fabrizio Romano posts a photo and quotes Kylian Mbappé on a possible El Clásico followed by the Ballon d'Or ceremony: "Let's go for it." Not checked here.
Entertainment outlet Deadline reports that Disney+ and Hulu have given a series order to a reboot of the TV show Glee. It says co-creator Ryan Murphy has discussed a return for some time.
Film news account DiscussingFilm says a third Star Wars: Battlefront game is in the works, with Respawn and DICE developing it together. It cites a source by link. Not checked here.

State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott says a report of ordered departures across Gulf embassies is inaccurate: the order covers non-emergency staff and families in Saudi Arabia only, citing Houthi attacks. The report was by Timour Azhari. Not checked here.

HQNewsNow posts a 15-second clip of President Trump saying "I'd say 90% of the reason I took the governor--" before he makes a loud noise. The clip does not show what he was answering. Not checked here.

Streamer QTCinderella says people were late to her wedding and that it set the wedding back. She asks viewers to stop hating on someone on behalf of another streamer and says drama clippers have farmed it. The post does not name who she means.
Enes Kanter Freedom says he was kicked out of a WNBA game for the second time in a row, and says it was for supporting women. Not checked here.
The Associated Press reports that Virginia state Sen. L. Louise Lucas is charged with drug trafficking and money laundering, citing the Justice Department. Not checked here.
Reporter Dan Lamothe says in an exclusive that Pete Hegseth wanted Gen. Dwight Eisenhower's globe for his office and that Hegseth's staff broke it. He says he has photos. Not checked here.

Polymarket, a prediction-market account, says Airbnb has announced new rules banning hosts from requiring guests to wash dishes, do laundry, strip beds or take out garbage before checkout. WIRED reports hosts are upset about the policy. Not checked here.

The HHS Rapid Response account says 15 of 15 New York adult daycares audited the day before showed no record of meals, activities or supervision, only attendance sheets, and calls it Medicaid fraud. The post carries a video. Not checked here.

Investor m. stanfield says an unnamed executive at a large property management company told him over dinner that the US apartment market is the worst that person has seen in 40 years. These are secondhand claims. Not checked here.

PopBase, an entertainment news account, says Getty Images has filed for bankruptcy amid mounting debt and competition from AI-generated images, and plans to restructure and become privately owned. Not checked here.
The account unusual_whales says the stock with the ticker $MRNA is down 24% today to $187 and describes options-market price levels it calls support and resistance. Not checked here.
The Hollywood Reporter reports that actor Tom Skerritt, a star of "Picket Fences" and "Alien", has died at 93. Not checked here.

Madison Mills, a reporter, posts an Axios scoop saying major US banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents inside customer accounts. Axios says it is told this by unnamed bank and industry executives. Not checked here.
Sky News posts a breaking alert saying Barclays is cutting 5,000 jobs in an efficiency drive led by AI. The post links to Sky’s own report. Not checked here.
